title: Relax reflection configuration errors for unresolved types.

timeline.body:
Fixes #1548.

Instead of throwing a hard error, display a warning and proceed
parsing the remainder. Useful for framework-type bits.

This is a good change but I think we should make it conditional on the `--allow-incomplete-classpath` option. And while we're here we should be consistent in how we treat the missing classes/fields/methods encountered during the parsing of reflection config. There are several locations in this file where we catch `NoClassDefFoundError` and show a warning. I think we should make those conditional too, i.e., show a warning if `--allow-incomplete-classpath` is set but throw an error otherwise. The error message should point to the `--allow-incomplete-classpath` option as we do in `SharedGraphBuilderPhase.reportUnresolvedElement()`. Additionally, the two instances of `NoSuchFieldException` and `NoSuchMethodException` that now throw an error should be treated similarly.
Right on, I'll follow these suggestions. Thanks!

timeline.message:
Relax reflection configuration errors for unresolved types.

Fixes #1548.

Instead of throwing a hard error, display a warning and proceed
parsing the remainder. Useful for framework-type bits.

Wrap warnings/errors in the allow-incomplete-classpath option.
timeline.author: Bob McWhirter

timeline.body: @peter-hofer should the `ReflectionConfigurationParser` instance in `com.oracle.svm.configure.config.ConfigurationSet.loadTypeConfig()` be configured with `allowIncompleteClasspath` too? The reflection config there is the result of profiling, could it stil throw on missing classes?

reply.body: That code only builds an in-memory reflection configuration without doing any lookups on the class path, so it should not throw.

timeline.body: I looked and a few other instances seemed to have no route to obtain a Hosted option.

I wonder why we currently only show warnings in some cases and fail fatally in others. Maybe there is a legitimate use case for that with which people could avoid using `--allow-incomplete-classpath` if they don't need it otherwise since it may conceal other problems during the build. @cstancu , you originally introduced those warnings, did you have a specific use case in mind back then?

@peter-hofer when this feature was initially implemented every exceptional case resulted in an error and we slowly started relaxing the restrictions over time for specific use cases. This was a long-awaited refactoring (thanks @bobmcwhirter)! I think that we can keep the restriction that missing elements in config files resulted from profiling will throw an error, at least until proven otherwise.

@bobmcwhirter this is now merged but the PR was not marked as merged automaticaly. I think that I pulled your PR in before the force-push, but I double checked and all changes are in the master: https://github.com/oracle/graal/commit/510a4aa02ccb83f4872d4b93d2407835f8869fd4 and https://github.com/oracle/graal/commit/a5698cd6280e15680341c444c2cb039d0ca206c1. I'll close this manually. Thank you!
